title: Alaska Purchase
summary: The United States acquired Russian North America, comprising present-day Alaska, from Russia for $7.2 million. A treaty was signed on 30 March 1867 and possession was taken on 18 October. Russia saw the territory as a costly liability; critics mocked it as "Seward's Folly", though Alaska later proved strategically and economically valuable.

as_recorded.value: the treaty was signed early the following day
The United States officially took possession on October 18

where.modern_name: Alaska, United States (proxy pin: centre of the territory purchased)

importance.justification: Major US territorial acquisition; Smithsonian ranks it second only to the Louisiana Purchase among American land deals.
